ELP (Extra Large Power Service) (City of San Antonio, Texas (Utility Company))

FIG. 01 — REFERENCE IMAGE

[ Photo: commercial utility meter ]

The Short Answer: ELP (Extra Large Power Service) (City of San Antonio, Texas (Utility Company)) is this is the official elp (extra large power service) commercial tariff offered by city of san antonio, texas (utility company) in dc. it includes specific demand (kw) charges based on peak usage. On a commercial bill, this line typically indicates shave peak exposure.

FIG. 02 — STRUCTURAL CONTEXT

Why Utilities Use This Model

This specific tariff is filed by City of San Antonio, Texas (Utility Company) with the DC public utility commission. It dictates exactly how your facility's energy and demand consumption is priced, and serves as the legal basis for your monthly commercial billing.

🧮 Worked Scenario

If your facility has a peak demand of 50kW and your tariff charges $10/kW (typical for a MID band), that single line item costs you $500/month, regardless of how many kWh you actually use.

FIG. 03 — COMMON ERRORS

The Common Misread

The most common mistake is assuming owners assume reducing total kwh will lower the demand charge, but demand is based on a single 15-minute spike. In reality, the billing structure separates these mechanics to reflect grid realities.

How to spot this: Check the top right corner of your bill for "Rate Schedule" or "Service Classification." Common codes include "GS-2", "E-19", or "Large TOU".

🎯 Your One Action This Week

Focus on shave peak. Review your last two bills to see if this specific lever is driving your costs.
